title: Britain Tried To Build An Aircraft Carrier Out Of Ice

segments.narration: Britain planned an aircraft carrier made entirely of ice. This was a funded project with drawings.
The problem was the mid-Atlantic gap, a stretch of ocean no land-based aircraft could reach. U-boats hunted freely inside it.
Geoffrey Pyke's answer was pykrete: fourteen percent wood pulp, the rest water. Frozen, it is far tougher than ice and melts slowly.
The design ran two thousand feet long and 2.2 million tons. A sixty-foot prototype sat on Patricia Lake in Alberta, chilled by one small motor.
Then long-range aircraft closed the gap, and the costings beat it. Real steel carriers were cheaper than a mountain of frozen sawdust.
